screeningSummary: Ham radio operator insists all sightings are ionosphere-heating experiments like HAARP
arcNotes: Opinion caller - confident, zero technical grounding (Fake). Vern delivers the real HAARP facts: Alaska facility, narrow upward beam, can't make visible lights, handed to a university. Invites him to actually use his radio for direction-finding

lines.text: Twenty years on the ham bands - then humor me with the actual HAARP, because I've got its file. One site, Gakona, Alaska. A hundred eighty antennas pointed straight up. Effective radiated power in the megawatts - impressive, until you learn it's a flashlight compared to the sun's constant push on the same sky. It makes faint airglow for instruments. It does not make lights a farmer sees from his porch in Ohio. It cannot. The physics won't sign off.

lines.text: You have twenty years of RF experience, so the specifications: HAARP is a single facility at Gakona, Alaska - one hundred eighty crossed dipoles, zenith-directed, effective radiated power on the order of megawatts. For comparison, solar input to the ionosphere exceeds it by many orders of magnitude. Its documented output is faint instrument-grade airglow. It cannot produce visible phenomena at continental distances; the energy budget prohibits it.
